skills.title: Map bank service dependencies
skills.trigger: A bank needs to understand which services fail with a branch, system or provider.
skills.inputs: Service catalogue, branch/channel scope and outage records
steps: Trace a customer service across branch, application, data and provider dependencies
Identify single points of failure and responsible roles
Agree service-specific recovery questions with the business owner
skills.acceptance: The business owner can trace an outage from dependency to affected service.

supporting_references.label: NRB IT Guidelines 2012 (historical instrument; check current applicability and amendments)

skills.title: Review bank access and conflicting powers
skills.trigger: A bank needs an evidence-backed access and segregation review.
skills.inputs: Role export, authorized policy, joiner/leaver records and synthetic transaction cases
steps: Map permissions to initiation, approval and reconciliation powers
Compare actual permissions with authorized duties and exceptions
Test allowed and prohibited actions only in an approved test environment
skills.acceptance: Every conflict or permission conclusion has actual evidence and an accountable reviewer.

supporting_references.label: NRB IT Guidelines 2012 (historical instrument; check current applicability and amendments)

skills.title: Assess bank branch technology readiness
skills.trigger: A bank is considering a new or changed branch service.
skills.inputs: Site survey, service hours, approved connectivity design and support responsibilities
steps: Map branch equipment and connectivity dependencies to critical services
Check observed site conditions and backup paths against the intended design
Record readiness gaps and acceptance tests before rollout
skills.acceptance: Readiness statements stay specific to the observed branch and approved service design.

skills.title: Plan a bank recovery exercise
skills.trigger: A bank needs to rehearse service recovery without disrupting live operations.
skills.inputs: Approved exercise scope, recovery targets, dependency map and restore evidence
steps: Define the failure scenario, permitted environment and abort conditions
Capture restore and reconciliation timestamps against agreed objectives
Separate measured recovery from planned capability and assign remediation
skills.acceptance: The exercise has explicit authorization, safe boundaries and measured results rather than assumed recovery.

supporting_references.label: NRB IT Guidelines 2012 (historical instrument; check current applicability and amendments)

skills.title: Review bank supplier exit readiness
skills.trigger: A bank depends on an outsourced service and needs a credible exit assessment.
skills.inputs: Contract, data/interface inventory, supplier commitments and authorized export test
steps: Trace operational and data dependencies on the provider and subcontractors
Identify export, transition, support and deletion evidence needed for exit
Test an approved representative export and record unresolved dependencies
skills.acceptance: Exit capability is supported by an actual test or remains explicitly unproven.

skills.title: Review a bank system migration
skills.trigger: A bank needs evidence before approving a release or data migration.
skills.inputs: Source/target mappings, change authority, test totals and rollback plan
steps: Define reconciliation invariants and rejected-record handling
Rehearse a representative migration in an isolated environment
Compare totals, duplicates, exceptions and rollback results before human go/no-go
skills.acceptance: A change decision traces to reconciled test results and unresolved exceptions.

skills.title: Structure bank incident triage
skills.trigger: A bank needs a factual incident record and response handoff.
skills.inputs: Authorized incident scope, logs, known service impact and response roles
steps: Preserve relevant timestamps and observations without exposing credentials
Separate confirmed impact from hypotheses and ongoing investigation
Record containment options and escalation for the authorized responder
skills.acceptance: The handoff preserves uncertainty and does not authorize unrequested production containment.

skills.title: Build a bank regulatory evidence crosswalk
skills.trigger: A bank needs to map an actual obligation to implementation evidence.
skills.inputs: Original instruments, applicability scope, amendments, internal policy and reviewer authority
steps: Identify the current instrument and exact provision for the entity and service
Trace each provision to control, actual evidence and owner
Escalate unresolved applicability and conflicting editions to qualified review
skills.acceptance: No compliance conclusion is produced from a historical guideline or an unreviewed checklist alone.

supporting_references.label: NRB IT Guidelines 2012 (historical instrument; check current applicability and amendments)
NRB policy and guideline index; identify instruments applicable to the actual institution

skills.title: Analyze digital banking channel failures
skills.trigger: A bank needs to investigate failed channel transactions or service errors.
skills.inputs: Defined channel, redacted event records, failure categories and reconciliation evidence
steps: Define a failure unit and time window without counting retries as new customers
Group observed failures and distinguish correlated from established causes
Reconcile failed, reversed and completed events before recommending a controlled next test
skills.acceptance: Counts and causal statements can be reproduced from the authorized evidence.

skills.title: Review bank audit remediation
skills.trigger: A bank needs to know which audit issues are actually closed.
skills.inputs: Original findings, agreed actions, responsible roles, target dates and closure tests
steps: Keep the original finding and authority separate from implementation claims
Trace action completion to independent closure evidence where required
Flag overdue or unsupported closure and retain residual risk decisions
skills.acceptance: Closed means the stated acceptance and review evidence exists, not merely that a ticket changed state.

skills.title: Map bank customer-data flows
skills.trigger: A bank needs to understand customer-data exposure across systems and providers.
skills.inputs: Authorized process map, data classes, system interfaces and permitted access scope
steps: Trace collection, use, transfer, storage and disposal for the selected process
Identify data owners and third-party access without copying customer records
Record the applicable institutional and legal review needed for each exposure
skills.acceptance: The map uses minimized references and does not disclose real customer data in public artifacts.

skills.title: Assess bank service capacity
skills.trigger: A bank needs capacity evidence for a specific channel or service.
skills.inputs: Observed workload, peak-window definition, latency/error measures and approved test limits
steps: Define service-level measures and a representative workload
Compare observed demand and tested capacity under explicit conditions
Document bottlenecks, uncertainty and a safe scaling or retest option
skills.acceptance: Capacity claims apply only to measured conditions and do not imply guaranteed future service levels.

skills.title: Match a tech-shop offer to a buyer need
skills.trigger: A small tech shop needs to prepare a relevant and supportable offer.
skills.inputs: Actual use case, budget authority, exact configuration and dated supplier evidence
steps: Separate the buyer problem from a preferred product name
Map required capabilities to exact variants and included services
Record exclusions, evidence gaps and quote validity before approval
skills.acceptance: No price, stock, compatibility or warranty is invented to fill the offer.

skills.title: Inspect received technology stock
skills.trigger: A shop needs to reconcile a delivery with its order.
skills.inputs: Purchase order, received items, exact variants, quantities and condition evidence
steps: Count received units and identify exact configurations
Trace damaged, missing or substituted units to the purchase record
Separate available, quarantined and unresolved stock states
skills.acceptance: The stock record reconciles to physical receipt and does not silently accept substitutions.

skills.title: Record repair authorization and custody
skills.trigger: A shop needs a safe, reviewable device intake.
skills.inputs: Device condition, accessories, fault description and customer authorization scope
steps: Record device identifier or UNKNOWN, custody timestamp, accessories, visible condition and the customer-reported symptom separately from a diagnosis
Record the authorized diagnostic scope and data-access consent reference before inspection; missing authorization blocks intrusive work
Define approval points before extra work or parts replacement
skills.acceptance: Work and data access remain within actual authorization and custody is traceable.

skills.title: Plan a bounded device diagnosis
skills.trigger: A technician needs to investigate a reported fault before promising repair.
skills.inputs: Authorized job scope, fault reproduction, device documentation and safe test conditions
steps: Reproduce the fault and record baseline observations
Choose non-destructive checks appropriate to the exact device and competence
Distinguish diagnosis, hypothesis and proposed repair with further-approval needs
skills.acceptance: No destructive repair, data access or electrical work is implied by a diagnostic plan.

skills.title: Verify a repaired device before return
skills.trigger: A shop needs evidence that agreed repair work was delivered.
skills.inputs: Authorized work, parts record, pre/post observations and agreed return tests
steps: Compare delivered work with the approved scope
Run agreed functional checks and record remaining faults
Reconcile accessories, custody and customer acceptance without claiming unsupported data recovery
skills.acceptance: The return record identifies what was tested, what failed and what remains excluded.

skills.title: Trace warranty and support responsibility
skills.trigger: A shop needs to handle a device or repair warranty case.
skills.inputs: Sale/job reference, exact warranty terms, reported fault and supplier route
steps: Distinguish the sold warranty from assumed manufacturer coverage
Trace eligibility and exclusions to actual documents
Record responsible parties, evidence and the next support action
skills.acceptance: Support promises match documented coverage and unresolved eligibility remains unknown.

skills.title: Build a traceable landed-cost worksheet
skills.trigger: A shop needs to compare acquisition cost scenarios.
skills.inputs: Dated supplier values, currency, logistics costs and current applicable tax/customs evidence
steps: Separate observed costs from scenario assumptions
Normalize currency, units and inclusion bases before comparison
Identify missing charges and sensitivity to exchange or delivery changes
skills.acceptance: The worksheet is a labelled cost scenario, not a fabricated market quotation or tax opinion.

supporting_references.label: Nepal tariff search; classification and effective rate require case-specific review

skills.title: Reconcile stock and movement records
skills.trigger: A shop needs to explain physical-to-record stock differences.
skills.inputs: Opening stock, receipts, sales, returns, adjustments and physical count
steps: Use consistent SKU and variant identifiers for every movement
Reconcile recorded closing stock with a dated count
Investigate exceptions without deleting the original movement evidence
skills.acceptance: Every unexplained variance remains visible and corrections have an authorized record.

skills.title: Plan replenishment from real stock history
skills.trigger: A shop needs a defensible replenishment decision.
skills.inputs: Actual demand history, stock states, supplier lead times and available cash
steps: Separate confirmed demand from enquiries and one-off projects
Estimate replenishment scenarios with observed lead-time and uncertainty
Compare cash and support constraints before an owner decision
skills.acceptance: A scenario does not become a purchase commitment or invented demand forecast.

skills.title: Normalize technology supplier offers
skills.trigger: A shop needs an apples-to-apples supplier comparison.
skills.inputs: Dated offers, exact variants, tax/inclusion terms and delivery/warranty evidence
steps: Resolve configuration and quantity differences first
Separate firm terms from advertised or unverified claims
Compare total included scope and unresolved commercial risks
skills.acceptance: No cheapest-offer conclusion hides different configurations or missing services.

skills.title: Review shop receivables and next actions
skills.trigger: A shop needs to follow up actual unpaid transactions.
skills.inputs: Authorized sales records, receipts, due terms and disputed balances
steps: Reconcile each balance before classifying age or status
Separate disputes, missing receipts and confirmed overdue items
Prepare a human-review follow-up list without contacting customers
skills.acceptance: No payment demand is sent and no unverified debt is asserted as fact.

skills.title: Review service-job economics
skills.trigger: A shop needs to understand the cost of a completed or proposed job.
skills.inputs: Actual or explicitly assumed labour, parts, delivery, support and revenue bases
steps: Separate cash movement from cost and revenue recognition assumptions
Normalize labour/time and included support obligations
Report scenario sensitivity and unresolved costs rather than inventing profit
skills.acceptance: Any margin is reproducible from labelled inputs and is not a guaranteed outcome.

skills.title: Establish a school technology need
skills.trigger: A school needs to define the teaching problem before choosing equipment.
skills.inputs: Teacher workflows, class context, current equipment/use and accessibility barriers
steps: Observe the selected teaching task and existing alternatives
Define a measurable intended change with actual operators
Separate a documented need from preference or vendor demonstration
skills.acceptance: A product purchase is not presented as proof of teaching need or learning benefit.

skills.title: Survey a classroom for technology installation
skills.trigger: A school needs evidence of room suitability.
skills.inputs: Actual room layout, intended users, sightlines, acoustics and mounting constraints
steps: Record room conditions and intended teaching positions
Test visibility, sound and interaction using an authorized representative setup
Escalate safety and accessibility issues before installation design
skills.acceptance: Room-readiness claims stay tied to the observed room and test conditions.

skills.title: Review school equipment power readiness
skills.trigger: A school needs to understand power constraints for proposed ICT.
skills.inputs: Equipment load information, site evidence, operating hours and competent safety review
steps: Map the intended load and power dependencies
Record measured/verified conditions separately from estimates
Define safe outage behaviour and unresolved professional checks
skills.acceptance: The assessment does not substitute for competent electrical design or certify safety.

skills.title: Assess school network requirements
skills.trigger: A school needs a network that supports actual teaching and administration.
skills.inputs: Users, rooms, applications, coverage observations and support capacity
steps: Map intended tasks to connectivity and access needs
Check observed coverage and shared-capacity constraints
Define acceptance tests and support ownership without promising unmeasured bandwidth
skills.acceptance: Network requirements follow actual workflows and measured or explicit unknown conditions.

skills.title: Verify school ICT funding and purchase stages
skills.trigger: A school or supplier needs to distinguish a plan from funded procurement.
skills.inputs: Institution identity, official budget/notice, fiscal year and amendments
steps: Trace each asserted stage to its own owning document
Keep allocation, fund release, procurement and award separate
Record missing approvals and current verification dates
skills.acceptance: No announcement or budget heading becomes a confirmed purchase or customer commitment.

skills.title: Draft outcome-based school ICT requirements
skills.trigger: A school needs a reviewable specification tied to teaching and operation.
skills.inputs: Teaching need, site constraints, accessibility needs and acceptance authority
steps: Translate tasks into measurable functional and operating requirements
Include installation, content rights, training and support requirements
Separate mandatory requirements from preferences with evidence bases
skills.acceptance: The draft does not invent approvals or disguise an unsupported brand restriction.

skills.title: Review educational content and software rights
skills.trigger: A school needs to understand what it may use and renew.
skills.inputs: Actual licence terms, content sources, account model and language/accessibility needs
steps: Identify the exact permitted use and user/device limits
Map renewal, offline use and data-sharing conditions to the teaching task
Record unsupported permissions and accountable renewal ownership
skills.acceptance: The review does not claim rights or included content without an actual licence basis.

skills.title: Map school account and student-data boundaries
skills.trigger: A school needs a minimal-data technology workflow.
skills.inputs: Institution policy, intended process, data classes, roles and provider terms
steps: Map required collection and user access for the selected task
Identify avoidable identifiers and external sharing
Prepare a permission/minimization review without publishing student records
skills.acceptance: No identifiable student dataset is inserted into a public example or research package.

supporting_references.label: Official IEMIS; use only data definitions applicable to the actual school study

skills.title: Design task-based teacher training
skills.trigger: A school needs training that operators can actually use.
skills.inputs: Teaching tasks, operator language/accessibility needs, available time and support route
steps: Select real tasks and common failure/exception cases
Prepare task practice and reference materials for actual operators
Record demonstrated capability separately from attendance
skills.acceptance: Attendance alone is not reported as successful adoption or capability.

skills.title: Review school ICT installation acceptance
skills.trigger: A school needs to decide whether delivered work meets the agreed scope.
skills.inputs: Approved requirements, exact delivered configuration, test plan and acceptance authority
steps: Reconcile equipment and services with the approved scope
Run agreed site and operator acceptance tests
Record defects, exclusions and authorized acceptance evidence
skills.acceptance: Equipment delivery is not automatically installation or teaching acceptance.

skills.title: Evaluate school technology usage claims
skills.trigger: A school or researcher needs to review use and outcome evidence.
skills.inputs: Usage definitions, baseline/follow-up periods, denominators and support records
steps: Distinguish installation, actual use and learning outcomes
Reconcile denominators and missing data before comparisons
Assess alternative explanations and report design limits
skills.acceptance: A usage increase is not automatically a causal learning improvement.

supporting_references.label: Official IEMIS; use only data definitions applicable to the actual school study

skills.title: Plan school ICT maintenance and renewals
skills.trigger: A school needs a sustainable support plan after installation.
skills.inputs: Asset/configuration records, warranty terms, subscriptions, staff capability and local support
steps: Identify recurring maintenance, renewal and replacement dependencies
Assign accountable roles and escalation routes
Define periodic checks and an evidence-based review schedule
skills.acceptance: The plan identifies actual support capacity rather than assuming the installer remains available.

skills.title: Bound a Nepal technology research question
skills.trigger: A researcher needs an answerable question and intended decision.
skills.inputs: Proposed topic, population, geography, timeframe and decision audience
steps: Define the unit and intended inference
Separate broad interest from a feasible answerable question
Record exclusions and evidence needed before analysis
skills.acceptance: The question has a defined scope and does not claim the research has already been done.

skills.title: Build a source-traceable literature matrix
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to establish an actual literature gap.
skills.inputs: Original studies, exact locators, designs, populations and conflicting findings
steps: Read relevant methods and findings in the original sources
Compare definitions, scope and limitations across studies
State the gap without treating search results as completed reading
skills.acceptance: A reviewer can trace the claimed gap to the actual sources and their limits.

skills.title: Review a research sampling plan
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to justify who or what is observed.
skills.inputs: Target population, available frame, inclusion rules, selection method and feasible resources
steps: Compare frame coverage with the intended population
Identify selection, non-response and missingness risks
Limit inference to the design and document any justified weighting/estimation needs
skills.acceptance: A convenience sample is not labelled representative of Nepal or every municipality.

skills.title: Review a research instrument pilot
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to test a questionnaire, observation or technical measurement instrument.
skills.inputs: Research constructs, draft instrument, respondent/operator context and pilot permission
steps: Map each item to the intended construct and analysis
Test comprehension, burden and measurement behaviour in an authorized pilot
Record changes and unresolved validity limits before main collection
skills.acceptance: Pilot convenience or face validity is not overstated as full instrument validation.

skills.title: Plan research permissions and data minimization
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to establish what may be collected and shared.
skills.inputs: Institution requirements, participant/system context, intended fields and access roles
steps: Identify required permissions and review authority before relevant collection
Minimize identifiers and define access/retention boundaries
Separate public reproducibility materials from confidential records
skills.acceptance: No collection permission or ethics approval is invented by the toolkit.

skills.title: Create a research data dictionary
skills.trigger: A researcher needs consistent definitions before combining or analysing data.
skills.inputs: Actual source schema, units, codes, periods, geography and access limits
steps: Preserve original variable names and definitions
Specify units, missingness, classifications and transformations
Version the dictionary and identify incompatible fields before joining
skills.acceptance: Each derived measure can be traced to defined original inputs and transformations.

skills.title: Audit research data transformations
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to explain how analysis data differs from source data.
skills.inputs: Authorized raw/derived versions, transformation code and exclusion rules
steps: Trace input versions through each transformation
Reconcile row counts, duplicates, missing values and exclusions
Record decisions without deleting contradictory evidence
skills.acceptance: Another researcher can reproduce the transformation and explain exclusions.

skills.title: Review Nepal research dates and calendars
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to compare records with BS, AD, fiscal and publication dates.
skills.inputs: Original date strings, calendar labels, reference periods and conversion evidence
steps: Preserve raw dates and identify the calendar and semantic date type
Verify any conversion with a suitable owning or validated source
Separate retrieval, publication, event and measurement periods
skills.acceptance: A URL year or retrieval date is not silently used as an event or observation date.

skills.title: Review Nepal locality joins
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to join local evidence without mixing places or boundaries.
skills.inputs: Owning locality codes, district/province context, boundary editions and aliases
steps: Resolve identity within its district and boundary version
Document aliases and unresolved matches
Check join cardinality and coverage before assigning local findings
skills.acceptance: National or provincial evidence is not relabelled as municipal or ward evidence.

skills.title: Check comparable denominators and units
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to compare rates or counts responsibly.
skills.inputs: Original numerator, denominator, unit, period, population and scope definitions
steps: Check that quantities refer to compatible units and populations
Normalize only justified conversions and retain original values
Explain exclusions and refuse unsupported adoption or market interpretations
skills.acceptance: Account counts are not treated as unique people and unmatched windows are not combined.

skills.title: Prepare a reproducible descriptive analysis
skills.trigger: A researcher needs a summary of observed data without unsupported inference.
skills.inputs: Authorized dataset, dictionary, scope, missingness and intended output
steps: Define the analysis population and summary statistic
Reproduce counts and distributions with explicit missing-data handling
Separate description from causal or population-wide claims
skills.acceptance: Every reported result is reproducible and bounded by the observed data.

skills.title: Review uncertainty and robustness claims
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to know which assumptions can change the conclusion.
skills.inputs: Study design, sample/measurement uncertainty, analysis choices and sensitivity results
steps: Identify material uncertainty and unsupported precision
Test feasible alternative definitions or assumptions
Report sensitivity and design limits rather than inventing confidence
skills.acceptance: Precision and confidence claims are justified by an actual method and evidence.

skills.title: Build a transparent qualitative coding record
skills.trigger: A researcher needs a traceable interpretation of authorized qualitative evidence.
skills.inputs: Research question, consented/redacted material, coding approach and reviewer roles
steps: Define a codebook and preserve context around extracts
Record coding decisions, disagreements and negative cases
Bound themes to the material and sampling design
skills.acceptance: Themes are traceable without publishing identifiable participant material or inventing prevalence.

skills.title: Review a proposed causal conclusion
skills.trigger: A researcher needs to distinguish an effect claim from association.
skills.inputs: Design, baseline, comparison, timing, confounders and alternative explanations
steps: Map the causal claim to the identification strategy
Examine selection, timing, concurrent changes and missing counterfactual evidence
Revise the conclusion to the strongest supported inference
skills.acceptance: A before-after change alone is not presented as proof of causation.

skills.title: Prepare a research reproducibility package
skills.trigger: A researcher needs another person to reproduce permitted outputs.
skills.inputs: Source/access rights, input versions, environment, code and expected outputs
steps: Separate distributable metadata/code from restricted data
Document exact transformations and execution steps
Record independent reproduction differences and correction actions
skills.acceptance: No restricted dataset or invented independent review is included to claim reproducibility.

skills.title: Audit research-report claims and citations
skills.trigger: A researcher needs a final check of methods, results and interpretation.
skills.inputs: Draft report, original evidence, calculation records and required format
steps: Trace material claims to original sources or reproducible analysis
Check quotation, scope, dates and contradictions
Separate findings, assumptions and recommendations before reviewer handoff
skills.acceptance: Unsupported or overgeneralized claims remain open rather than being polished into apparent fact.

skills.title: Qualify a Nepal ICT procurement notice
skills.trigger: A supplier needs to decide whether a notice deserves full review.
skills.inputs: Official notice, procuring entity, scope, dates and accessible documents
steps: Establish the exact entity and substantive ICT scope
Distinguish notice type and procurement stage
Record missing documents and a justified pursue/review/exclude decision
skills.acceptance: Incidental computer terminology is not enough to qualify unrelated work.

supporting_references.label: Official e-GP portal; retrieve the actual notice, amendments and issuer documents

skills.title: Verify procurement deadlines and submission conditions
skills.trigger: A bidder needs a reliable deadline and submission checklist.
skills.inputs: Actual bid document, amendments, original dates, timezone and submission route
steps: Extract each deadline with its clause and calendar
Resolve amendments and verify any date conversion
List remaining security, location and procedural uncertainties for human review
skills.acceptance: No deadline or conversion is inferred from an unrelated publication timestamp.

supporting_references.label: Official e-GP portal; retrieve the actual notice, amendments and issuer documents

skills.title: Build a bidder eligibility matrix
skills.trigger: A bidder needs to check documentary and organizational eligibility.
skills.inputs: Full current bid document, actual bidder evidence and amendment history
steps: Extract exact requirements and their scope
Map each to actual dated bidder evidence
Flag missing, expired, partial or conflicting records before a human bid decision
skills.acceptance: The matrix does not invent authorizations, experience, turnover or eligibility.

supporting_references.label: PPMO goods procurement documents; choose the applicable procedure and actual bid documents

skills.title: Extract a technology BOQ with traceability
skills.trigger: A supplier needs a reliable item/quantity/specification working sheet.
skills.inputs: Original BOQ pages, schedules, units, specifications and amendments
steps: Retain item numbering, raw descriptions, units and quantities
Link technical requirements and commercial inclusions by clause
Reconcile totals and flag OCR or ambiguous rows
skills.acceptance: No unreadable quantity, omitted row or OCR guess is silently accepted as verified.

supporting_references.label: PPMO goods procurement documents; choose the applicable procedure and actual bid documents

skills.title: Review exact-model technical compliance
skills.trigger: A bidder needs evidence for an offered model and included configuration.
skills.inputs: Actual tender clauses, exact manufacturer model/SKU and authoritative configuration documents
steps: Separate base, optional and supplied features
Map each requirement to an exact document/version and locator
Record deviations and evidence gaps without claiming equivalent compliance automatically
skills.acceptance: Compatibility, an optional feature and official approval remain distinct claims.

supporting_references.label: PPMO goods procurement documents; choose the applicable procedure and actual bid documents

skills.title: Reconcile bid amendments and document versions
skills.trigger: A bidder needs to know which requirement or deadline is current.
skills.inputs: Original documents, official amendments, issue dates and affected clauses
steps: Identify the authoritative version chain
Map each amendment to changed clauses, dates and schedules
Retain unresolved conflicts for clarification
skills.acceptance: A later amendment is not omitted merely because an older downloaded file is easier to read.

supporting_references.label: Official e-GP portal; retrieve the actual notice, amendments and issuer documents

skills.title: Prepare a procurement clarification request
skills.trigger: A bidder needs a concise source-linked clarification draft.
skills.inputs: Exact ambiguous clauses, conflicting evidence and authorized communication route
steps: State the ambiguity without alleging unsupported intent
Explain its bid/design consequence with document references
Draft a precise question for human review without sending it
skills.acceptance: No official communication is sent or procuring-entity approval fabricated.

supporting_references.label: Official e-GP portal; retrieve the actual notice, amendments and issuer documents

skills.title: Review final bid readiness and unresolved gaps
skills.trigger: A bidder needs a reviewable go/no-go packet.
skills.inputs: Eligibility, technical, commercial, deadline and approval records
steps: Reconcile checklist items to actual final bid artifacts
Identify unresolved dependencies, deviations and required signatures
Prepare the authorized decision packet without submitting a bid
skills.acceptance: A completed checklist does not itself authorize submission or assert an award.

supporting_references.label: Official e-GP portal; retrieve the actual notice, amendments and issuer documents

skills.title: Compare technology offers on lifecycle scope
skills.trigger: A buyer needs to compare offers beyond headline price.
skills.inputs: Exact configurations, installation/training scope, licence/support terms and dated costs
steps: Normalize functional and commercial inclusions
Separate acquisition, recurring and replacement assumptions
Compare lifecycle scenarios and unknowns for the buyer decision
skills.acceptance: A low headline price is not called best value when scope or operating costs differ.

skills.title: Translate a technology contract into delivery obligations
skills.trigger: A delivery team needs an actionable contract handover.
skills.inputs: Executed/authorized contract, schedules, requirements and responsibility records
steps: Trace scope, deliverables, dependencies and evidence obligations
Identify change authority and acceptance/payment conditions
Assign unresolved interpretations to the authorized contract owner
skills.acceptance: The handover does not invent contractual terms or authorize a variation.

supporting_references.label: PPMO goods procurement documents; choose the applicable procedure and actual bid documents

skills.title: Inspect a technology delivery against agreed scope
skills.trigger: A buyer or integrator needs a traceable delivery discrepancy record.
skills.inputs: Approved order/contract, actual delivered items, variants and condition evidence
steps: Reconcile item identity, quantity and included components
Record damage, substitutions and missing services
Separate goods receipt from installation and final acceptance
skills.acceptance: Physical receipt is not treated as full contract or technical acceptance.

supporting_references.label: PPMO goods procurement documents; choose the applicable procedure and actual bid documents

skills.title: Trace acceptance evidence to payment conditions
skills.trigger: A project owner needs to check whether payment conditions are evidenced.
skills.inputs: Actual contract conditions, tests, acceptance authority, invoices and defect records
steps: Match each payment condition to the required acceptance evidence
Reconcile completed work, unresolved defects and authorized decisions
Prepare a review packet without committing payment or certifying completion
skills.acceptance: No payment commitment or completion certificate is generated from missing evidence.

supporting_references.label: PPMO goods procurement documents; choose the applicable procedure and actual bid documents

skills.title: Trace technical requirements to verification
skills.trigger: An engineering team needs a testable requirements baseline.
skills.inputs: Actual users/tasks, constraints, source requirements and acceptance authority
steps: Define measurable functional and nonfunctional requirements
Map each to design and verification evidence
Retain unresolved assumptions and change ownership
skills.acceptance: Every material requirement has a testable verification route or an explicit unresolved gap.

skills.title: Compare architecture options for a Nepal deployment
skills.trigger: A team needs an architecture decision suited to its workload and operating capacity.
skills.inputs: Workload, data sensitivity, connectivity, team capability and operating constraints
steps: Define decision criteria before selecting vendors or patterns
Compare feasible options and failure/recovery dependencies
Record assumptions, trade-offs and a reversible validation step
skills.acceptance: An architecture is not recommended solely because it is fashionable or used elsewhere.

skills.title: Review an integration API contract
skills.trigger: A team needs predictable interfaces and failure handling.
skills.inputs: Current endpoint/schema documentation, authorized test environment and data ownership
steps: Specify identity, payload, version and error semantics
Test valid, rejected, duplicate and retried requests within scope
Record reconciliation and compatibility gaps
skills.acceptance: A successful happy-path request is not treated as complete integration acceptance.

supporting_references.label: HTTP response status codes; use for the actual HTTP API contract

skills.title: Rehearse an application data migration
skills.trigger: A team needs evidence before migrating an actual system.
skills.inputs: Authorized copy, source/target schema, invariants and rollback authority
steps: Define safe test data and transformation mappings
Run an isolated rehearsal and reconcile counts/content
Test rejected records and restoration before a release recommendation
skills.acceptance: No rehearsal command is applied to production without separately authorized scope.

supporting_references.label: PostgreSQL backup and restore; applicable only to PostgreSQL and the deployed version

skills.title: Verify a representative backup restore
skills.trigger: A team needs evidence that selected data can actually be restored.
skills.inputs: Backup scope, authorized isolated environment, recovery target and integrity checks
steps: Choose a representative permitted restore case
Record timing and compare restored content with expected invariants
Document losses, dependencies and retest actions
skills.acceptance: A backup job success or file presence is not accepted as proof of recoverability.

supporting_references.label: PostgreSQL backup and restore; applicable only to PostgreSQL and the deployed version

skills.title: Review application authentication and authorization boundaries
skills.trigger: A team needs to test access appropriate to actual roles.
skills.inputs: Role/action matrix, session/token design and authorized test cases
steps: Separate authentication from permission decisions
Exercise permitted, forbidden, signed-out and cross-user cases safely
Record evidence and remediation without exposing credentials
skills.acceptance: Testing stays authorized and does not infer security from a login screen alone.

supporting_references.label: HTTP cookies; one browser/session mechanism, not a complete authorization policy

skills.title: Review data exposure in a technical design
skills.trigger: A team needs to minimize data collection and unintended disclosure.
skills.inputs: Data classes, purpose, flows, provider access and retention requirements
steps: Trace sensitive data through collection, storage, logs and export
Identify unnecessary fields and access paths
Define evidence needed for minimization and applicable institutional review
skills.acceptance: The design review does not publish private records or claim legal compliance automatically.

supporting_references.label: Web privacy guidance; does not establish Nepal legal compliance

skills.title: Build a scoped technical threat review
skills.trigger: A team needs a practical threat and mitigation assessment.
skills.inputs: System boundaries, assets, actors, trust boundaries and actual deployment context
steps: Map plausible threats to concrete exposure and consequence
Review existing controls and their evidence
Choose validation actions and accountable residual-risk decisions
skills.acceptance: Threat hypotheses are not reported as confirmed compromises or calibrated probabilities.

skills.title: Review software dependencies and update readiness
skills.trigger: A team needs to understand dependency/version exposure before changing software.
skills.inputs: Actual manifests, locked versions, owning advisories and supported runtime requirements
steps: Reconcile installed/declared versions and dependency scope
Check relevant owning advisories and compatibility evidence
Prepare a tested update/rollback plan with unresolved risks
skills.acceptance: An advisory mention is not automatically a confirmed exploitable condition in the actual system.

skills.title: Prepare a recoverable release checklist
skills.trigger: A team needs a reviewable release decision.
skills.inputs: Exact change, test evidence, migration state, deployment target and rollback plan
steps: Identify the target and current baseline before release
Map change-specific tests and dependencies to evidence
Record authorized go/no-go criteria and recovery verification
skills.acceptance: A local build or passing unit test is not reported as a deployed and verified release.

skills.title: Prepare an actionable service incident runbook
skills.trigger: A team needs a response plan matched to actual services and authority.
skills.inputs: Service map, observed failure modes, escalation roles and approved actions
steps: Define detection and triage evidence for the selected service
Separate read-only checks from actions needing authorization
Include abort, escalation, recovery and post-incident evidence
skills.acceptance: The runbook does not silently authorize destructive or production-affecting actions.

skills.title: Review operational logging and sensitive-data exposure
skills.trigger: A team needs useful diagnostics without unnecessary data leakage.
skills.inputs: Current log fields, access/retention configuration and incident questions
steps: Map each logged field to an operational purpose
Identify secrets, identifiers and excessive retention/exposure
Define redaction, access and diagnostic acceptance checks
skills.acceptance: Useful observability is not obtained by retaining credentials or unrestricted private payloads.

skills.title: Review a technology workflow for accessibility
skills.trigger: A team needs evidence that actual users can complete a workflow.
skills.inputs: Selected tasks, interface, user needs, accessibility standards and test context
steps: Define critical tasks and relevant interaction modes
Inspect keyboard, labels, focus, errors and content barriers
Record reproducible failures and user/task acceptance criteria
skills.acceptance: Automated checks alone are not described as exhaustive accessibility certification.

supporting_references.label: Web accessibility guidance; test actual task flows and applicable requirements

skills.title: Establish a reproducible application performance baseline
skills.trigger: A team needs a meaningful baseline before optimization.
skills.inputs: Actual workload, environment, data volume and service-level definitions
steps: Define repeatable measurement conditions and success/error measures
Run only authorized bounded tests
Report distributions, bottlenecks and limits before proposing a change
skills.acceptance: A single fast response is not presented as a general capacity or latency guarantee.

skills.title: Review a database query and its evidence
skills.trigger: A team needs to improve a query without changing result meaning.
skills.inputs: Exact query/schema/version, representative permitted data and execution evidence
steps: Confirm intended result semantics and access boundaries
Inspect execution evidence and relevant indexes/constraints
Compare correctness and performance in a safe test environment
skills.acceptance: An optimization cannot silently change result correctness or run unsafe writes in production.

supporting_references.label: PostgreSQL EXPLAIN; applicable only to the actual database/version

skills.title: Review data-pipeline integrity
skills.trigger: A team needs to detect and explain broken or misleading data ingestion.
skills.inputs: Source contract, transformation versions, reconciliation rules and job evidence
steps: Trace ingestion through validation and transformation stages
Test missing, duplicate, late and rejected records
Preserve provenance and distinguish empty results from failed collection
skills.acceptance: A failed fetch or parser is not reported as evidence that no underlying records exist.

skills.title: Prepare a network addressing and dependency plan
skills.trigger: A team needs a documented network design for actual sites and users.
skills.inputs: Site inventory, current topology, address usage, service boundaries and support constraints
steps: Reconcile actual addresses and dependencies
Identify overlap, segmentation and connectivity requirements
Define controlled validation and rollback for proposed changes
skills.acceptance: A proposed network change is not treated as safe or deployed without site-specific verification.

skills.title: Review an endpoint configuration baseline
skills.trigger: A team needs manageable endpoint settings suited to actual users.
skills.inputs: Device/OS versions, role needs, update/support state and institutional policy
steps: Map settings to user tasks and threats
Check observed configuration and support evidence
Prepare role-appropriate remediation and recovery tests
skills.acceptance: A generic hardening list is not applied blindly to every device or claimed compliant.

skills.title: Design service monitoring with actionable signals
skills.trigger: A team needs alerts that support response rather than noise.
skills.inputs: Service objectives, failure modes, available telemetry and response coverage
steps: Map signals to user-visible failure and actionable thresholds
Define alert ownership and permitted diagnostic steps
Test an alert-to-response path and document blind spots
skills.acceptance: A configured dashboard is not described as verified continuous monitoring without operating evidence.

skills.title: Prepare an engineering support handover
skills.trigger: A team needs another operator to maintain the delivered system.
skills.inputs: Actual configuration, versions, access authority, recovery procedure and support responsibilities
steps: Reconcile handover material to delivered and tested behaviour
Include common tasks, failure handling and renewal dependencies
Have an authorized operator demonstrate essential tasks and record gaps
skills.acceptance: Documentation delivery alone is not proof that operations can maintain or recover the system.

skills.title: Plan technology customer discovery
skills.trigger: A Nepal technology business needs to test a problem and buyer hypothesis.
skills.inputs: Defined segment, problem hypothesis, consent-based research plan and observed alternatives
steps: Separate user, buyer and budget authority
Design neutral questions about actual behaviour and constraints
Record contradictory evidence and next validation steps without inventing demand
skills.acceptance: An interview preference or friendly reaction is not counted as a paying customer commitment.

skills.title: Build evidence-based technology buyer segments
skills.trigger: A business needs segments useful for delivery and sales decisions.
skills.inputs: Observed needs, buying processes, support reach and available institutional data
steps: Choose segmentation variables tied to actual decisions
Check whether evidence supports the proposed distinctions
Record reachable scope and validation gaps
skills.acceptance: National population or all registered institutions are not treated as immediately reachable buyers.

skills.title: Build a bounded technology-market scenario
skills.trigger: A business needs a bottom-up market assessment.
skills.inputs: Verified buyer counts, eligibility/use cases, purchase frequency and explicitly sourced cost/price assumptions
steps: Define the addressable population and exclusions
Separate total, eligible, reachable and funded/current buyers
Calculate labelled scenarios and sensitivity without inventing numbers
skills.acceptance: A scenario is not presented as measured demand or a guaranteed revenue forecast.

skills.title: Define a supportable ICT service offer
skills.trigger: A business needs an offer aligned with actual delivery capacity.
skills.inputs: Buyer problem, deliverables, delivery limits, evidence and support responsibilities
steps: Define the outcome, included work and explicit exclusions
Check every promise against actual capability and evidence
Set acceptance, change and support boundaries for human approval
skills.acceptance: The offer does not invent clients, guarantees, certifications or delivery capability.

skills.title: Prepare a technology lifecycle cost scenario
skills.trigger: A business needs a transparent cost model for a proposed service or system.
skills.inputs: Actual quotes or labelled assumptions, units, periods and operating obligations
steps: Separate upfront, recurring and replacement cost bases
Normalize consistent periods/currency and inclusion assumptions
Show missing inputs and sensitivity before a spending decision
skills.acceptance: The model is not a quotation, financing recommendation or invented market price.

skills.title: Review a technology project cash cycle
skills.trigger: A business needs to see payment timing and funding gaps.
skills.inputs: Actual contract/payment terms, supplier obligations, expected timing bases and known balances
steps: Distinguish recognized revenue/profit from cash timing
Map dated inflows and outflows to evidence or explicit scenarios
Identify timing mismatches and owner decisions without committing finance
skills.acceptance: No unsupported cash balance, payment certainty or financial commitment is fabricated.

skills.title: Audit technology marketing claims
skills.trigger: A business needs public copy that its delivery evidence supports.
skills.inputs: Draft copy, exact product/service scope and actual proof records
steps: Classify material claims by the evidence they need
Check compatibility, certification, client, price and outcome wording
Revise unsupported wording and retain required human approval before publication
skills.acceptance: Good wording does not convert an unsupported claim into a verified one.

skills.title: Prepare a source-backed technology campaign brief
skills.trigger: A business needs useful marketing tied to a real buyer problem.
skills.inputs: Target audience, problem evidence, supported offer and channel constraints
steps: Define the buyer action and evidence-backed message
Select a format suitable to the actual audience and resources
Prepare creative requirements and a measurement plan without posting
skills.acceptance: No fabricated result, urgency, client or endorsement is added to improve persuasion.

skills.title: Compare channels for a Nepal technology offer
skills.trigger: A business needs to choose where to spend marketing effort.
skills.inputs: Audience evidence, channel observations, available resources and matched outcome measures
steps: Define the decision and comparable measurement windows
Separate observed results from expectations and attribution claims
Compare feasible tests and missing data rather than guaranteeing a channel
skills.acceptance: Unmatched periods or platform claims are not treated as reliable comparative returns.

skills.title: Qualify an institutional technology opportunity
skills.trigger: A sales team needs a factual next-step decision.
skills.inputs: Actual need evidence, decision roles, funding/procurement stage and support reach
steps: Separate a signal or enquiry from a verified opportunity
Check technical fit, authority, timing and reachable delivery
Record qualification gaps and the next authorized action
skills.acceptance: A relationship, public budget or news story is not counted as a confirmed sale.

skills.title: Build a reviewable technology proposal
skills.trigger: A business needs a proposal that traces promises to evidence.
skills.inputs: Actual requirements, supported solution scope, delivery evidence and commercial assumptions
steps: Map each proposed deliverable to the buyer need and supporting evidence
Define dependencies, exclusions, acceptance and support
Flag unapproved prices/commitments for human review
skills.acceptance: The proposal does not invent success stories, approvals or commercial commitments.

skills.title: Plan technology project dependencies
skills.trigger: A project team needs a feasible sequence and accountable handoffs.
skills.inputs: Actual deliverables, site conditions, resources, procurement stages and acceptance roles
steps: Identify dependencies before assigning dates
Separate assumed availability from confirmed constraints
Define phase exits, owners and unresolved blockers
skills.acceptance: A schedule does not imply approvals, resource availability or completion that has not been evidenced.

skills.title: Assess staffing capacity for a technology service
skills.trigger: A business needs job-relevant capability and coverage planning.
skills.inputs: Actual workload, role duties, service hours, skills evidence and lawful staffing constraints
steps: Map tasks to required capability and coverage
Distinguish training, experience and demonstrated task performance
Document gaps and practical staffing/training scenarios without judging sensitive personal traits
skills.acceptance: A role plan is not an automated hiring decision or fabricated employee-performance claim.

skills.title: Review a technology delivery partner
skills.trigger: A business needs to verify what a partner can actually supply and support.
skills.inputs: Exact proposed role, authorized credentials, delivery evidence and geographic support scope
steps: Map responsibilities and dependencies between parties
Check claimed capability and authority against actual evidence
Record gaps, escalation and acceptance boundaries before commitment
skills.acceptance: A partner claim or reseller relationship is not treated as an OEM authorization or delivery guarantee.

skills.title: Define actionable business and operating metrics
skills.trigger: A team needs metrics that can be calculated and interpreted consistently.
skills.inputs: Actual decision, source fields, periods, units and responsible data owners
steps: Define numerator, denominator and inclusion rules
Trace collection and missingness to actual systems
State how the metric informs a decision and what it cannot establish
skills.acceptance: A polished dashboard number is not trusted without a reproducible definition and evidence.

skills.title: Prepare technology-business scenarios and monitoring questions
skills.trigger: A Nepal technology business needs to plan around uncertainty.
skills.inputs: Actual dependencies, relevant external signals, base evidence and owner decisions
steps: Define plausible scenarios and their explicit mechanisms for the business
Separate observed signals from assumptions and predictions
Specify trigger evidence and review actions without inventing probabilities
skills.acceptance: A scenario or discovered source is not presented as a forecast or a running monitor.
